unit: science/physics-paper-1 (Unity College, AQA Combined Science: Trilogy)

findings.claim: there are eight energy stores in the AQA specification
findings.truth: The spec never lists or numbers energy stores, and student-facing text must not name the board. Reworded to 'there are eight energy stores you need to know'.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.1.1 (a grep for 'energy store' returns no enumerated list); house rule on naming the board

findings.claim: In AQA Combined Science, calculation questions on energy are very common.
findings.truth: Board named in student-facing text. Reworded to 'In Combined Science'.
findings.evidence: house rule on naming the board

findings.claim: A light bulb, for example, transfers energy from the chemical store of the mains supply to light (useful) and thermal energy (wasted).
findings.truth: The mains supply is not a chemical store. Energy reaches the lamp electrically, and the waste goes to the thermal store of the surroundings.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.1.1 lists the transfers as heating, work done by forces, and work done when a current flows

findings.claim: Both students transfer the same amount of energy: Eₗ = mgh = 2 x 9.8 x 1.5 = 29.4 J
findings.truth: The symbol for gravitational potential energy is Eₚ, not Eₗ. The arithmetic itself is right (29.4 J, then 9.8 W and 19.6 W).
findings.evidence: spec Appendix B equation 9: Ep = m g h; recomputation 2 x 9.8 x 1.5 = 29.4

findings.claim: The 'Reducing Unwanted Energy Transfers' section (lubrication, thermal insulation) sits inside a div with class higher-only.
findings.truth: This is core content for both tiers. Only 'describe ways to increase the efficiency of an intended energy transfer' carries the (HT only) flag. Wrapper removed, opening and closing tags together.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.2.1 has no HT flag on lubrication and thermal insulation; spec 6.1.2.2 marks the efficiency statement (HT only)

findings.claim: Tidal power is the only major energy resource whose original source is not the Sun.
findings.truth: Geothermal energy and nuclear fuel are not Sun-derived either. Reworded to say only that tidal power is driven by the Moon's gravity, not by the Sun.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.3 lists nuclear fuel and geothermal among the main energy resources; settled fact

findings.claim: Understanding the advantages and disadvantages of each type is a key part of the AQA spec.
findings.truth: Board named in student-facing text.
findings.evidence: house rule on naming the board

findings.claim: Three data-revision-tip prompts are rotated by one: the conservation key fact asks for the efficiency equation, the efficiency key fact asks for fossil fuels, and the non-renewables key fact asks about efficiency.
findings.truth: Each tip rewritten to match the key fact it is attached to. No tip added or removed.
findings.evidence: internal: each key-fact text against its own data-revision-tip

findings.claim: AQA Required Practical 4 asks you to investigate the I-V characteristics of different circuit components.
findings.truth: On this course the I-V practical is required practical 16, not 4. Number 4 is the separate-physics numbering. Reworded to 'One of your required practicals', so no number or board is asserted.
findings.evidence: spec 10.2.16 (I-V characteristics); 10.2.14 specific heat capacity, 10.2.15 resistance, 10.2.17 density

findings.claim: A 'Calculating Total Resistance in Parallel' box teaches 1/Rtotal = 1/R1 + 1/R2 with a worked example, the exam tip tells students to find 1/Rtotal first, and the 6-mark question asks for the total resistance of three parallel lamps.
findings.truth: The spec says students are not required to calculate the total resistance of two resistors joined in parallel. The physics and the arithmetic are correct (6 and 12 give 4 ohms; three 6-ohm lamps give 2 ohms), so this is stretch content presented as examinable. Options: (a) keep the box but label it as extension, delete the exam-tip sentence and rewrite the 6-mark question; (b) cut the box outright. Either ripples through narration n27 to n31.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.2: 'Students are not required to calculate the total resistance of two resistors joined in parallel.'

findings.claim: resistors: A measure of how much a component opposes the flow of current, measured in ohms.
findings.truth: That defines resistance, not a resistor. Redefined as a component whose resistance is measured in ohms. The same wrong definition sat in the flashcard deck and the glossary.
findings.evidence: settled definition

findings.claim: The UK mains electricity supply is a.c. with a frequency of 50 Hz and a peak voltage of about 230 V.
findings.truth: 230 V is the value the spec gives for the supply, not the peak. The peak is about 325 V. Reworded to 'a potential difference of about 230 V'.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.3.1: 'the domestic electricity supply has a frequency of 50 Hz and is about 230 V'

findings.claim: This means the current changes direction 50 times every second.
findings.truth: 50 Hz means 50 complete cycles per second, so the current reverses 100 times per second. Reworded to 'completes 50 full cycles every second'.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.3.1 (50 Hz); settled definition of frequency

findings.claim: It alternates between approximately +230 V and -230 V (repeated in the live-wire definition and the glossary).
findings.truth: The same peak error as F12: 230 V is the supply value, not the swing limit. Reworded to say the potential difference swaps sign and is about 230 V compared with earth.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.3.2: 'The potential difference between the live wire and earth (0 V) is about 230 V'

findings.claim: This equation is on the AQA physics equation sheet. (density = mass / volume)
findings.truth: Density is equation 21 in the recall list, so students must be able to recall and apply it. It is not on the equation sheet, and a student who trusts this will not learn it. Reworded to 'You must be able to recall this equation.'
findings.evidence: spec Appendix B recall list equation 21; the equation sheet carries only v2-u2=2as, Ee=0.5ke2, E=mc(temp change), T=1/f, F=BIl, E=mL and VpIp=VsIs

findings.claim: Density calculation questions are common on AQA Physics Paper 1
findings.truth: Board named in student-facing text.
findings.evidence: house rule on naming the board

findings.claim: activity: The number of radioactive decays detected per second, measured using a Geiger-Muller tube.
findings.truth: That is the spec definition of count-rate. Activity is the rate at which a source of unstable nuclei decays, measured in becquerels. The spec separates the two terms. Corrected in the definition and the glossary.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4.2.1: 'Activity is the rate at which a source of unstable nuclei decays... Count-rate is the number of decays recorded each second by a detector (eg Geiger-Muller tube).'

findings.claim: Only about 119 years have passed since 1898
findings.truth: 1898 to 2026 is about 128 years. Reworded to 'Little more than a century has passed since 1898' so it cannot go stale again. The 1600-year half-life and the Curie attribution are both right.
findings.evidence: arithmetic: 2026 - 1898 = 128

findings.claim: Because radium emits all three types (alpha, beta, gamma), the notebooks pose a hazard at close range and at a distance.
findings.truth: Radium-226 itself is an alpha emitter with a weak gamma. The beta emissions come from its decay-chain daughters, which are present in an old contaminated sample, so the conclusion stands. No edit.
findings.evidence: settled fact; the spec sets no decay-chain detail

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches static charge, earthing, uses and dangers of static electricity, and electric field patterns.
findings.truth: None of this is in the Combined Science spec. Topic 6.2 stops at the National Grid; static electricity and electric fields are separate-physics content. The physics taught is correct and the numbers check out (E = QV = 2.0e-6 x 50000 = 0.1 J). Options: (a) keep it, labelled as separate-science extension that is not examined here; (b) move it to the separate-sciences subject row and drop it from this unit. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2 runs 6.2.1 to 6.2.4 with no static charge or electric field section

findings.claim: potential difference: The voltage between a charged object and the earth, which increases as more charge builds up.
findings.truth: That is one special case, not the definition of potential difference, and it contradicts the correct definitions in lessons 3 and 5. Redefined as energy transferred per unit charge, with the dome-to-earth case named as the example.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.1.3; the lesson 3 definition

findings.claim: The lesson teaches Boyle's law with pV calculations, pressure in a column of liquid (p = h x rho x g), atmospheric pressure and upthrust.
findings.truth: For this qualification the particle model and pressure section is qualitative only: explain how molecular motion relates to temperature and pressure, and the relation between temperature and pressure at constant volume. pV = constant, pressure in fluids, atmospheric pressure and upthrust are separate-physics. The calculations are all correct (800 kPa, 450 kPa, 24500 Pa). Options as for F20. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 6.3.3.1 Particle motion in gases carries qualitative bullets only, and 6.3 has no fluids or atmospheric pressure section

findings.claim: This links to AQA and is a key concept for understanding how gases behave when conditions change.
findings.truth: Garbled sentence that also names the board. Reworded.
findings.evidence: house rule on naming the board

findings.claim: The content opens with two nested divs that both carry class higher-only.
findings.truth: Duplicated wrapper. One opening tag and its matching closing tag removed, so the section keeps a single Higher-tier flag.
findings.evidence: internal: the first two lines of content_html and the two closing tags before the Atmospheric Pressure heading

findings.claim: 'You may also see kilopascals (kPa) used, where 1 kPa = _____ Pa' with the answer '1000'
findings.truth: A cloze fragment lifted from the body. A one-word answer needs a question that starts What, Which, Who, When or Name. Rewritten as 'What is 1 kilopascal (kPa) equal to in pascals?'
findings.evidence: house flashcard rule

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches background radiation, medical and industrial uses of radiation, nuclear fission, chain reactions, reactor components and nuclear fusion.
findings.truth: Topic 6.4 for this qualification stops at 6.4.2.4 (radioactive contamination). Background radiation, uses of radiation, fission and fusion are separate-physics. The content itself is sound (radon the largest UK source, technetium-99m with a 6-hour half-life, 800 Bq to 100 Bq over three half-lives). Options as for F20. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4 contents: 6.4.1 Atoms and isotopes, then 6.4.2.1 to 6.4.2.4 only

findings.claim: The final section, 'Star Formation and the Life Cycle of Stars', teaches nebulae and the main sequence.
findings.truth: Even on the separate-physics course this is Space physics, which sits on Physics Paper 2, not Paper 1. It is the weakest fit of anything in the unit and is the first thing to cut if lesson 11 is kept. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4 carries no space content; the assessment section puts topics 18 to 21 on Physics Paper 1

findings.claim: Two cards are body-text fragments: '_____ sources account for roughly 85% of background radiation' and '_____ sources make up the remaining 15% and include medical procedures (X-rays, CT scans, radiotherapy), nuclear weapons testing fallout, and nuclear power station discharges'
findings.truth: One-word answers ('Natural', 'Artificial') need questions that start What, Which, Who, When or Name. Both rewritten as What-questions.
findings.evidence: house flashcard rule

findings.claim: Nuclear fission of uranium can yield the same 2.5 MWh from just 2.5 grams of uranium.
findings.truth: The coal figure (about 2.5 MWh of electricity per tonne) is right. The uranium mass cannot be pinned down: complete fission of pure uranium-235 matches a tonne of coal at roughly 0.3 g, while the usual fuel-pellet comparison uses about 7 g of enriched fuel. 2.5 g sits between the two and the spec is silent, so no edit.
findings.evidence: the spec is silent; recomputation from standard energy densities gives 0.3 g to 7 g depending on the basis

summary: 11 lessons checked: 29 findings (2 HIGH, 12 MEDIUM, 15 LOW) and 35 edits. Every calculation in the unit recomputes correctly and every knowledge-check key is right. The damage is two wrong exam claims (230 V called the peak mains voltage; density said to be on the equation sheet when it is in the recall list) plus five scope problems: lessons 9, 10 and 11 are separate-physics content that this qualification does not carry, and the parallel-resistance formula in lesson 4 is explicitly excluded by the spec.
